providers.title: The canonical trace on matrices over the reduced group C*-algebra
providers.scope: tau(ab) = tau(ba); tau is positive and faithful on positive elements; tau(I_n) = n. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The trace on K_0
providers.scope: Equivalent projections have equal traces, tau induces a homomorphism tau_*: K_0(C_r*(G)) -> R, and a nonzero projection has a nonzero class. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A projection of irrational trace (OpenAI)
providers.scope: There are a finitely generated group G_sur, a prime p > 2, integers k_i with k_(i+1) - k_i -> infinity and a projection b_0 in C_r*(G_sur) of trace sum_i p^(-k_i); proved in lessons 2 to 7. Uses (EXP) and (OSA).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Sparse sums of powers are irrational
providers.scope: If k_(i+1) - k_i -> infinity, then sum_i p^(-k_i) is irrational, for every integer p >= 2. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Failure of the reduced Baum-Connes conjecture (OpenAI)
providers.scope: The class of b_0 is not in the image of the assembly map of G_sur. Uses Theorem 4.1 and (LUCK).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Walks below the girth
providers.scope: In a simple graph of girth sigma with a reduced labelling, a nonempty closed walk without backtracking has length at least sigma, and the label of a walk without backtracking is freely reduced. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Distinct copies
providers.scope: Copies with different indices share no simple path of length at least lambda sigma. Under the standing hypotheses (H1) to (H5) on the labelled graphs.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Minimal fillings
providers.scope: In a minimal filling no face has a freely trivial label, faces are at least as long as the girth of their copy, and no edge separates two faces or a face and an adjustable side of the same copy. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Short arcs and their number
providers.scope: In a minimal filling of a closed walk with m sides, arcs between different copies are shorter than lambda sigma, F <= m - 1 and b <= 6m. Under the standing hypotheses (H1) to (H5) on the labelled graphs.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Avoidance
providers.scope: A walk of length L in the coned graph between two vertices of a copy P that avoids its center gives d_P <= 12(L+1) lambda sigma(P). Under the standing hypotheses (H1) to (H5) on the labelled graphs.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Simplicity of the Cayley graph
providers.scope: If lambda < 1/12, the Cayley graph has no loops and no multiple edges. Under the standing hypotheses (H1) to (H5) on the labelled graphs.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Short fillings
providers.scope: Every closed walk of length n in the coned graph is a product of at most 12n conjugates of closed walks of length at most four. Under the standing hypotheses (H1) to (H5) on the labelled graphs.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Thin triangles with a universal constant
providers.scope: Geodesic triangles in the coned graph are D_0-thin, with D_0 = 10^6 independent of all the data; thin triangles from chain fillings are Lemma 2.1 of the lesson Thin triangles, overlap balls and the residual forest of the course kadison-kaplansky-projections. Under the standing hypotheses (H1) to (H5) on the labelled graphs.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Simultaneous overlaps (OpenAI)
providers.scope: Seen from a root R, all vertices that a copy P shares with copies whose centers are no farther from R lie in one intrinsic ball of P of radius floor(12(L_0+1) lambda sigma(P)). Under the standing hypotheses (H1) to (H5) on the labelled graphs.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Edge expansion from a spectral gap
providers.scope: If dI - Adj >= rho off the constants on a finite connected d-regular graph, then |dW| >= (rho/2) min(|W|, n - |W|). No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Logarithmic diameter
providers.scope: Edge expansion kappa gives diameter at most 2(log n / log(1 + kappa/d) + 1). No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Tree balls
providers.scope: In a d-regular graph of girth sigma, a ball of radius r with 2r + 1 < sigma is a tree with 1 + d sum_(j<r) (d-1)^j vertices. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The data (OpenAI)
providers.scope: There are labelled 4-regular expanders Theta_i satisfying (H1) to (H5) with a uniform spectral gap, small tree balls and k_i = floor(n_i/2) with k_(i+1) - k_i -> infinity. Uses (EXP) and (OSA).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Direct sum of copy cycles (OpenAI)
providers.scope: The space of finite cycles of the Cayley graph over F_2 is the direct sum of the cycle spaces of the copies. Uses (EXP) and (OSA).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Counting subspaces
providers.scope: Among the a-dimensional subspaces of an N-dimensional space over F_p, the proportion containing a given nonzero vector is (p^a - 1)/(p^N - 1). No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Codes with both distances (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For n_i > 100 there is a code of dimension floor(n_i/2) containing the prototype pattern such that every nonzero vector of the code and of its dual has support larger than n_i/100. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Exact relations (OpenAI)
providers.scope: The relations of all copies together impose on a single copy P exactly the dual code C_P^perp. Uses Lemma 3.1 of the lesson on thin triangles and Proposition 2.1 of the lesson on labelled expanders, hence (EXP) and (OSA).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The group G_sur
providers.scope: V x| Gamma is a countable group generated by (v_*, 1) and the (0, s), s in S, and its nonzero elements of V have order p. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Uniform pattern marginals (OpenAI)
providers.scope: Under the product measure on the dual of V, the pattern on a copy of type i is uniformly distributed on its code; it equals the prototype with probability p^(-k_i). Uses Lemma 2.1.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Fourier decomposition
providers.scope: The left regular representation of V x| Gamma is unitarily equivalent to the direct integral of the representations pi_omega on l^2(Gamma); norms are suprema over omega and the trace is the average of the diagonal coefficient at 1. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The operator in each representation
providers.scope: pi_omega(T) is the Laplacian dI - Adj(G_omega) of the enabled graph, with 0 <= pi_omega(T) <= 2dI. Uses Proposition 1.2 of the lesson on thin triangles.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deficit inside an invalid copy (OpenAI)
providers.scope: Every vertex set B of a copy that is not valid satisfies d|B| - 2e(B) >= c|B|. Uses Lemma 1.2 and Lemma 3.1 of the codes lesson and Proposition 2.1 of the lesson on labelled expanders.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deficit on the remaining graph (OpenAI)
providers.scope: Every finite set Y of vertices outside the valid copies satisfies d|Y| - 2|E(A)| >= (c/2)|Y| for the enabled edges A inside Y. Uses Lemma 3.1, the cycle-space decomposition and the simultaneous overlap bound, hence (EXP) and (OSA).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Uniform spectral gap (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For every omega the spectrum of pi_omega(T) lies in {0} together with [epsilon, 2d], epsilon = min(rho, c^2/(8d)), and its kernel is spanned by the indicators of the valid copies. Uses Lemma 3.2 of the Fourier lesson.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A projection in the reduced algebra (OpenAI)
providers.scope: b_0 = chi(T) is a projection in C_r*(G_sur) whose image in every pi_omega is the kernel projection of pi_omega(T). Uses Lemma 1.1 and the continuous functional calculus.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The trace (OpenAI)
providers.scope: tau(b_0) = sum_i p^(-k_i). Uses Proposition 2.1, Lemma 3.1 of the codes lesson and the trace formula of the Fourier lesson.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
